To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the test statistic is not consistent if the number of outlying observations depends on the sample length and that a test of discordancy based on a suitable transformation of this statistic is almost consistent.

1) the number of outliers is not constant but depends on the sample length, 2) the asymptotic distributions of a transformation of the test statistics are given by a mixture of chi-squared distributions and 3) if the number of outlying observations is not too large the test statistic has almost a consistent behaviour.
the use of a test statistic that is not robust to outliers can result in the rejection of the null hypothesis when it is actually true.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: 1.
the asymptotic behaviour, as n tends to infinity, of a test of discordancy in a time series, if the number and the position of the outliers are unknown.
the asymptotic behavior of a test statistic for discordancy in time-series, where both the sample size and the number of outliers are increasing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results obtained are of great interest for the statistical theory and practice, as well as for the applied sciences.
the asymptotic distribution of the transformed test statistic is a mixture of the distribution of a standard normal variable and a distribution with a mass point at zero.
the test statistic is consistent for a fixed number of outliers, but not for a growing number of outliers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the test of discordance for increasing sample size is almost consistent.
we have developed a new class of tests of discordancy for time series.
the asymptotic distribution of the statistic is not affected if the outliers are not too many.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in order to detect the presence of an outlier in a time series, it is necessary to have a large number of observations, if the number $p$ of outliers is not small.
the test is almost consistent, i.e. the test statistic is asymptotically distributed as a chi-square distribution, if the number outliers increases with increasing sample size.
the test of discordance is not consistent for increasing number of outliers, but it is almost consistent for a small degree of contamination.
